audit_findings.title: FY2026 anchor may retain a nonrecurring $328 million litigation settlement
audit_findings.magnitude: $328m pretax, equal to 96.1% of the $341.2m anchor OE; valuation effect unquantified pending trace
audit_findings.mechanism: The settlement can inflate OE through the FY2025 gain or the FY2026 receivable collection and may also remain within cash added in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The $328 million of income recognized in 2025 relates to the settlement of agreements to resolve credit card interchange fee litigation matters, net of legal fees.
audit_findings.explanation: The settlement's amount, nonrecurring nature, receivable recognition and subsequent $328m cash collection are demonstrated. Retention in anchor OE is unresolved because the OE calculation is not supplied. Given that the settlement nearly equals the entire anchor, even partial retention is reasonably capable of changing every scenario and the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $328m gain, associated taxes, FY2025 receivable increase and FY2026 cash collection through each OE worksheet period. Then rerun all scenarios after excluding the benefit exactly once and preventing any bridge double count.

audit_findings.title: Terminal value may capitalize credit-card economics beyond the contracted term
audit_findings.magnitude: $669m FY2025 and $172m Q1 FY2026 net credit-card revenue; post-2030 OE contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF growth path and terminal value perpetuate OE containing credit-card economics beyond the March 31, 2030 contract expiration and possible three-year renewal.
audit_findings.evidence: The Program Agreement expires March 31, 2030, subject to an additional renewal term of three years .
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual cutoff and present credit-card revenue are demonstrated, while renewal and post-contract economics are unresolved. Credit-card revenue was 196.1% of anchor OE, and terminal value represents 49.7% of base operating PV, so unsupported continuation is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Isolate the credit-card program's contribution to anchor OE, obtain the renewal provisions and concentration economics, and rerun scenarios with separately supported revenue, expense and profit-share assumptions after March 2030 and after any three-year renewal.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat required seasonal liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $1.294bn, or $4.64 per diluted share and 21.3% of the $6.088bn base equity value; required reserve unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments to operating PV even though cash required for seasonal working capital is an operating asset rather than distributable surplus.
audit_findings.evidence: Our working capital requirements fluctuate to support the seasonal nature of our business, increasing in mid-summer in anticipation of the fall merchandising season and increasing substantially prior to the months of November and December when the Company carries significantly higher inventory levels.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the full $1.294bn balance is demonstrated, as is the seasonal working-capital requirement. The necessary reserve is unresolved. Because the gross bridge addition exceeds the base valuation's $1.22-per-share shortfall to the market price, a reasonable reserve could change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum operating cash from monthly or weekly cash balances, peak inventory funding, payables, payroll, letters of credit and purchase obligations. Rerun the bridge adding only cash exceeding that reserve.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded SERP may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $415m obligation, $40m FY2025 benefits paid and $1.49 per diluted share gross claim; net valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If SERP payments are absent from projected OE, the unfunded obligation should enter the equity bridge as a senior claim; deducting it would reduce equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has a funded defined benefit pension plan ("the Pension Plan") and an unfunded defined benefit supplementary retirement plan ("SERP").
audit_findings.explanation: The $415m unfunded obligation and $40m annual cash payment are demonstrated. Whether OE already captures those payments is unresolved, and the separate $549m pension surplus is not shown to be legally available to the SERP. The gross claim equals 6.8% of base equity value and would reduce bull value from $23.83 to about $22.34 per share if deducted in full, so it can change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace SERP benefit payments through historical and anchor OE, obtain plan-specific assets and payment projections, and rerun either with explicit finite future payments in OE or a bridge deduction for the uncovered obligation—but not both.

audit_findings.title: Repeated restructuring cash costs may have been stripped as one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: $37m FY2025 and $59m FY2024 cash restructuring payments, equal to 10.8% and 17.3% of anchor OE; recurring valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing the entire impairment and restructuring caption can improperly add back recurring cash severance and closure costs to OE and capitalize the overstatement through the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The $ 230 million, $ 171 million and $ 1,027 million of impairment, restructuring and other costs, recognized in fiscal years 2025, 2024 and 2023 primarily relate to actions that align with Bold New Chapter.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash payments are demonstrated, while their treatment in OE is unresolved. Noncash impairments can be excluded, but cash restructuring payments of this scale are reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion if omitted from sustainable OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each year's $230m, $171m and $1.027bn captions into noncash impairment, cash restructuring and other items; trace the $37m and $59m payments through OE; then rerun with recurring cash costs retained or explicitly forecast.

audit_findings.title: Real-estate monetization could be counted both as earnings and bridge cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $48m FY2025 and $15m Q1 FY2026 gains; $107m FY2025 and $25m Q1 FY2026 net proceeds; lost store OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Value is overstated if disposition gains remain in OE while sale proceeds remain in bridge cash, or if OE retains earnings from assets removed from the operating perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: Asset sale gains in both 2025 and 2024 primarily reflect the monetization of non-go-forward store locations.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains, proceeds and ongoing store monetization are demonstrated, but neither double counting nor the earnings lost with sold or closed locations is established from the supplied OE record. The known amounts can affect value, while the null perimeter prevents determining the net material effect.
audit_findings.action: Trace every disposition gain out of OE, reconcile proceeds and related taxes or closure costs into cash, identify which sold properties generated operating earnings, and rerun using one consistent post-disposition operating perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $9.5m FY2017 residual, or 0.9% of filed D&A; about $134m or $0.48 per share under the base DCF sensitivity if fully eligible and recurring
audit_findings.mechanism: Any eligible residual D&A would be added back to OE, increasing operating PV and equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $1048.0m (99.1% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The identified $1.048bn already covers 99.1% of FY2017 filed D&A. Even treating the entire approximately $9.5m residual as a recurring eligible add-back would increase base value by only about 2.2%, from $21.83 to approximately $22.31 per share, still below the $23.05 market price. The uncertainty is conservative and does not change the stated conclusion.
audit_findings.action: No valuation rerun is required unless filed asset-level evidence classifies the residual as eligible and shows it recurs in the anchor period; if so, add back only the supported amount.
